subject: Figure reproducibility: storing data frame in ggplot object (?)

messages.author: 7e0eb6a1dcbfe39c
messages.subject: Figure reproducibility: storing data frame in ggplot object (?)
parts:
Hi, 
I've been using ggplot2 for a year now and I am really satisfied, both for the quality of the figures produced by R+ggplot2 and also for its intuitive and powerful syntax. I'm a scientist and a common problem in my community is the possibility to reproduce figures created in the past in order to update them or compare with up-to-date results. I was thinking about the possibility to create a "save" function that create both a figure file (e.g. png) and a metadata file with the raw data shown into the figure. Why not offering this possibility into ggplot2? In this way I would use ggplot + ggsave to save both data and figures, 
do you think another (user friendly and standardizable) way to achieve this goal?

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Figure reproducibility: storing data frame in ggplot object (?)
parts:
Hi:

When you create a "figure file", it gets saved onto disk, not in the R
workspace. By the same token, you can save an output file onto your
disk. You can always write an R function that saves both the graph and
the data to separate files. For more control over where those objects
get saved, you can include a function argument that specifies the
directory/folder to which they get saved.

If you want to keep the ggplot object and the data file yoked in the R
workspace, have your function return a list object.

Dennis
